transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I feel like I just can’t settle in my own body anymore. It’s especially bad when I’m supposed to sit quietly and deal with paperwork or make household plans with someone. I get restless and it’s been hard to manage.
Did you have this kind of restlessness as a child?

Yes, I think so. Looking back, it was there in elementary school. I was the kid with the messy desk and forgotten permission slips, and teachers would send notes home that I talked out of turn or couldn’t seem to stay in my seat.
As a child, did these problems also happen at home, not just at school?

I’m not completely sure. I remember the school stuff more clearly because teachers pointed it out. At home, I don’t have a clear memory either way — I’d probably have to ask my family what they noticed.
Do these problems happen in more than one part of your life now, such as both at work and at home?

Yes. I’m not working right now, but it definitely happens in more than one place. At home, people can’t really count on me the way they should, and it’s also affected things I do with volunteer groups. I’ve had to step back from some responsibilities because I keep dropping the ball, even when I’m really trying not to.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high or unusually irritable?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think I’ve had a time where my mood was unusually high. Irritable, maybe at times, but I’d have to think about what you mean by unusually.
Have you ever had a period when you had much more energy than usual?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I’m more productive or restless, but I can’t think of a clear period where I had way more energy than usual.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things?
I don’t know that I’d call it excessive. I worry about normal stuff, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed it being constant or taking over every day.
Did these problems begin or get noticeably worse after a major stressful or traumatic event in your life?
I wouldn’t say it was after a traumatic event. It’s been noticeably worse since I got married and our routines kind of merged, which was about a year and five months ago.
When you feel restless, does it usually come with feeling nervous or on edge?

Not usually nervous, exactly. It’s more like I can’t settle in my own body, especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and deal with paperwork or household plans. I get restless, but it doesn’t always feel like anxiety.
